issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodos() function. Direct string interpolation in SQL query allows attackers to inject malicious SQL code. Example: passing '; DROP TABLE todos; -- as keyword would execute destructive commands.
issues.suggestion: Replace string interpolation with parameterized queries: const query = `SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $2`; const searchPattern = `%${keyword}%`; const rows = await db.query(query, [searchPattern, searchPattern]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus() function. String concatenation allows arbitrary SQL execution. Attackers could pass '1 OR 1=1' to bypass filters or '1; DELETE FROM todos; --' to execute malicious commands.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries and validate input: const sql = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const rows = await db.query(sql, [completed]); Also validate that completed is a valid boolean value.

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser() function. Template literal string interpolation in JOIN query allows SQL injection. Example: passing ' OR '1'='1 would return all todos regardless of user, violating data isolation.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: const query = `SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1`; const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]);

issues.description: Missing input validation in searchTodos(). Function accepts any string without validation or sanitization. Empty strings, excessively long strings, or special SQL wildcards (%, _) could cause performance issues or unexpected behavior. Existing codebase uses validateTodoInput and sanitizeInput helpers.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: if (!keyword || keyword.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error('Search keyword cannot be empty'); } if (keyword.length > 100) { throw new Error('Search keyword too long'); } const sanitized = sanitizeInput(keyword);

issues.description: Type safety issue in searchTodosByStatus(). Function accepts string parameter for 'completed' when it should be boolean. This creates type confusion - developers might pass 'yes', 'no', 'true', 'false', '1', '0', leading to inconsistent behavior and SQL errors.
issues.suggestion: Change parameter type to boolean: export async function searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]> { const sql = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const rows = await db.query(sql, [completed ? 1 : 0]); return rows as Todo[]; }

issues.description: Missing error handling in searchTodos(). No try-catch blocks for database query failures. Database connection issues, timeouts, or constraint violations could crash the application or leak sensitive error information.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling: try { /* query logic */ } catch (error) { logger.error('Failed to search todos', { keyword, error }); throw new Error('Unable to search todos. Please try again.'); }

issues.description: Missing error handling in searchTodosByStatus(). Database errors will propagate as unhandled promise rejections.
issues.suggestion: Implement try-catch error handling with appropriate logging and user-friendly error messages.

issues.description: Missing error handling in getTodosByUser(). JOIN queries can fail for various reasons (foreign key constraints, connection issues) but no error handling exists.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive error handling with logging for database operations.

issues.description: LIKE query with leading wildcard '%keyword%' prevents database from using indexes on title and description columns. This forces full table scans, causing slow queries as the todos table grows.
issues.suggestion: Consider full-text search or provide option for prefix-only searches: const pattern = prefixOnly ? `${keyword}%` : `%${keyword}%`; Or use database full-text search: const query = `SELECT * FROM todos WHERE MATCH(title, description) AGAINST($1)`;

issues.description: Missing JSDoc documentation for searchTodosByStatus(). Function has vulnerability warning comment but lacks proper documentation explaining expected parameter values, return type, and behavior. Existing codebase uses JSDoc comments.
issues.suggestion: Add complete JSDoc: /** * Searches todos by completion status * @param {boolean} completed - Whether to search for completed (true) or incomplete (false) todos * @returns {Promise<Todo[]>} Array of todos matching the specified status * @throws {Error} If database query fails */

issues.description: Inconsistent naming convention. Function named 'getTodosByUser' uses 'get' prefix while other search functions use 'search' prefix. This inconsistency makes the API harder to discover and understand.
issues.suggestion: Rename to match established pattern: export async function searchTodosByUser(userId: string): Promise<Todo[]>

issues.description: Missing return value validation in all three functions. Type assertions (as Todo[]) bypass TypeScript's type safety without runtime validation. If database schema changes or returns unexpected data, this could cause runtime errors.
issues.suggestion: Add runtime validation: if (!Array.isArray(rows)) { throw new Error('Unexpected database response format'); } Optionally validate each row conforms to Todo interface.

codeQuality.summary: Critical security issues found. This PR introduces 3 critical SQL injection vulnerabilities through string interpolation/concatenation in SQL queries, completely bypassing the parameterized query pattern used in the existing codebase. All three new functions lack input validation, error handling, and proper type safety. The code quality represents a significant regression from established security best practices. Required actions before merge: replace all SQL string interpolation with parameterized queries, add input validation, fix type signature for searchTodosByStatus to use boolean, and add comprehensive error handling.

refactorings.summary: The three new functions deviate significantly from established security and code quality patterns in the existing codebase. Critical refactorings needed: (1) Replace all SQL string interpolation with parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection, (2) Add input validation and sanitization consistent with existing createTodo patterns, (3) Change searchTodosByStatus to accept boolean instead of string for type safety, (4) Extract common query execution pattern to reduce duplication. The existing codebase demonstrates security best practices (parameterized queries, input validation, sanitization) that these new functions completely ignore, creating a significant security regression. Risk of NOT refactoring: High - SQL injection vulnerabilities are exploitable and could lead to data breaches, unauthorized access, or data loss.

recommendations.description: IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED: Replace all SQL string interpolation and concatenation with parameterized queries in searchTodos(), searchTodosByStatus(), and getTodosByUser(). All three functions have critical SQL injection vulnerabilities that allow arbitrary SQL execution. Use the pattern: db.query(query, [param1, param2]) instead of string interpolation.

Add comprehensive test coverage for all three new search functions. Currently 0% test coverage. Minimum 16 critical/high priority tests needed covering SQL injection prevention, input validation, error handling, empty results, null/undefined inputs, and core functionality verification.

Add input validation and sanitization to all three search functions consistent with existing patterns in createTodo(). Validate for empty strings, null/undefined, excessively long inputs, and special SQL characters. Use existing sanitizeInput() helper function.

Change searchTodosByStatus() parameter from string to boolean. Current implementation accepts string which allows invalid values ('yes', 'maybe', etc.) causing SQL errors. Update signature to: searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]>

Add try-catch error handling to all three search functions. Database queries can fail due to connection issues, timeouts, or constraint violations. Implement proper error handling with logging and user-friendly error messages to prevent application crashes.

Extract common query execution pattern into shared helper function to reduce code duplication. All three functions follow identical pattern of query execution and result casting. This will provide a single point for adding logging, monitoring, or additional error handling.

Add complete JSDoc documentation to all three functions explaining parameters, return types, error conditions, and usage examples. Follow the documentation pattern established in the existing codebase.

Consider performance implications of LIKE queries with leading wildcards ('%keyword%'). This prevents index usage and forces full table scans. Evaluate implementing full-text search or providing options for prefix-only searches for better scalability.
